facts.fact: UNDP's 2025 annual report for the IDT4M project says 'work has commenced on the development of Malawi's National Digital Transformation Strategy', building on the Digital Readiness Assessment, through a consultative process; its 2026 plans say 'following its development' the strategy will guide digital investments across government, so it was not yet complete at the end of 2025.

At the Cabinet Retreat on Digital Transformation and AI in Mangochi, 28 to 30 November 2025, the report records 'high-level political endorsement of a unified digital roadmap', including the Minister of ICT's 'commitment to launch the National Digital Strategy' and, elsewhere, 'the relaunch of the National Digital Transformation Strategy'; no approval or adoption of a text by Cabinet is stated.

The report records the Malawi Cabinet Retreat of 28 to 30 November 2025, with UNDP support, ending in endorsement of a national digital roadmap, a commitment to launch the strategy and the creation of a Cabinet-level Digital Coordination Committee chaired by the Vice President (a 2026 plan item separately says the project will support its 'establishment and operationalization').

systems.owner: Ministry of ICT and Department of e-Government, with UNDP support; the report describes a national roadmap for digital public infrastructure, service delivery and digital governance, covering interoperability, cybersecurity, data governance, digital inclusion and emerging technologies
Department of e-Government with UNDP; AI Landscape Assessment started as its baseline
Ministry of Information and Digitalization, Department of e-Government and UNDP; launched 15 May 2025, scoring Malawi 2.7 out of 5, 'opportunistic' stage
DPI Safeguards Taskforce; draft to be validated at a national workshop
named only in the project results framework as a planned legal and operational framework
